correctness.rationale: For cell unions P=D and complements P=W\D, equality forces min and max of each target-cell mass to coincide. Omitting a selector of one point from every positive nonsingleton target cell forces one source row to simultaneously put all those cell masses at the omitted points. Conversely, selector rows avoid every partially included cell and attain exactly the probability of the E-interior. For the supremum defect, restrict arbitrary partial cells by chosen omitted points and compare their omitted mass with the full-selector maximal omitted mass; the reverse inequality is reached by an event missing exactly one point in every positive nonsingleton cell. Under support on C the d source rows must realize all d Dirac masses and thus are a permutation matrix. Independent exact-rational enumeration considered all partitions and all denominator-two stochastic matrices on n<=3; 2,188 cell/matrix pairs, no counterexample, including the defect identity.
